prompt: Indigestion remedies containing magnesium hydroxide relieve excess stomach acidity. What reaction is responsible?

options.text: The alkali dissolves food so the stomach empties faster
The hydroxide neutralises some hydrochloric acid in the stomach, forming a salt and water and raising the pH toward neutral
The remedy coats the stomach so acid can no longer be made
The magnesium absorbs acid into its crystals and carries it away unchanged

explanation: Magnesium hydroxide is a base. It neutralises excess hydrochloric acid — base + acid gives a salt plus water — which raises stomach pH and relieves the burning sensation of excess acid.
